headline: The winning lineup is already unavailable
body:
Cody won by eighteen hundredths last week. That lineup cannot simply return: Omarion Hampton’s Chargers are on bye. Chase Brown and Kaelon Black currently occupy the running-back slots where Hampton and Austin Ekeler produced 7.6 between them. At least one replacement is imposed by the schedule. The snapshot does not explain the other, and I will not improve Cody’s management philosophy on his behalf.

There is a second complication against McConkey Kong. Ja’Kobi Lane is currently selected at flex, with Emeka Egbuka on the bench. Egbuka and Carnell Tate supplied 30.3 last week, enough to do considerable repair work elsewhere. One of the sections that held the team together is changing too. These are the present selections, not confirmation that every replacement will be available or that the lineup is finished.

Sandy is 3–3 after a win powered by Tyler Shough and Christian McCaffrey. Both remain selected, McCaffrey now at flex. Cody is 4–2 despite scoring less over the season than Sandy. I am less interested in another prosecution of that record than in where the next win’s production will come from. The previous arrangement required a rescue and is unavailable for an encore. This one has to find its own way through.

headline: The bench has advice. It is not necessarily good advice.
body:
There are two ways to read a bench after a loss. Alan has moved C.J. Stroud into Gimothy Blossoms’ quarterback slot after Stroud outscored Bryce Young last week. Bennett still has Tre Tucker on Tranimal’s bench after Tucker scored 26.2 there. One conspicuous number has changed address. The other remains exactly where the postmortem found it.

Neither move explains its author. A Week 7 selection can reflect an opponent, availability or information the old box score cannot supply. And the Week 6 receipts are less commanding than they look. Stroud alone would not have rescued Alan. Even moving Tucker into MarShawn Lloyd’s flex spot would have left Bennett behind his brother. Both losses had more going on than the loudest number on the bench.

Bennett’s current flex pair is DK Metcalf and Bucky Irving; Alan’s is A.J. Brown and Denzel Boston. Those are the decisions to follow now, along with whether the quarterback choice holds through lock. Alan is 2–4, Bennett 4–2. There is plenty of urgency without asking either man to manage a game that has already ended. Last week’s points have one excellent quality: we know exactly what they are. Unfortunately, they are unavailable for this matchup.

headline: Three names, no game
body:
RFK Jr’s Bears has Josh Allen at quarterback, Dalton Kincaid at tight end and Jakobi Meyers at flex in the retrieved Week 7 lineup. Their clubs, Buffalo and Jacksonville, are on bye. Three occupied slots are not the same thing as three usable starters.

The returned roster contains no second quarterback or second tight end. Those positions require more than rearranging the bench; the flex slot also needs attention. A later roster change may already have supplied an answer. The captured selection is not evidence that Jason intends to accept three zeros, and it is not a finished team against which to judge Bryan’s chances.

Bryan has Kyle Pitts selected after the enormous tight-end bench gap in last week’s eighteen-hundredths defeat. There is a real change to inspect there, but the more immediate issue belongs to the other side. The Bears are 3–3; T. Ocellus is 2–4. Bryan can draw level on record with a win. First I want to see the opponent’s completed lineup. A filled-in form can conceal unfinished work.

headline: Keep the useful part
body:
Corey and Patrick are both 2–4, but the identical record conceals a useful disagreement about what needs replacing. Corey lost with the league’s second-highest Week 6 score. Patrick won while Bo Nix supplied 4.48. A policy of changing the loser and preserving the winner would be an exceptionally poor way to read these two rosters.

Corey currently retains Brock Bowers at tight end and Isaiah Likely at flex, the pairing that produced 29.9 last week. He has changed a running-back selection: Tyrone Tracy is in, while last week’s 22.7 from Bhayshul Tuten now belongs to a player on the bench. Patrick keeps Colston Loveland and Matthew Golden selected after they supplied 34.9 between tight end and flex. These are selections to verify, not claims that last week’s points will recur.

The interesting allocation is the flexible one. Corey is still spending a flex slot on a second tight end; Patrick is preserving room for Golden alongside Woody Marks. Corey has outscored Patrick by 66.58 over six weeks and has no additional wins to show for it. This meeting offers no refund. It does offer both men a chance to keep the parts that worked without insisting that the previous result certified the whole machine.

headline: The favorite is doing more rearranging
body:
Moe is 1–5 and currently has the same eight offensive starters selected as last week. Andrew is 4–2 and has changed both flex selections. The standings suggest which household ought to be moving the furniture. The lineups have not followed the suggestion.

For Jerruh’s World, Saquon Barkley and Roschon Johnson currently occupy the flex slots that belonged to Tyler Warren and Ryan Flournoy. Moe still has Mike Evans and Travis Kelce there, with Jordan Love at quarterback and RJ Harvey alongside Rico Dowdle at running back. Love and the two backs supplied 40.74 last week. There was something functional inside the defeat, even if it did not produce the second win.

There is an immediate requirement before the broader comparison: Moe still has Cam Little selected at kicker. Jacksonville is on bye, and no reserve kicker appears in the returned roster. The offensive selections may hold once availability is settled; the kicker cannot contribute in this matchup as selected. Andrew has three more wins and the better scoring total. Moe has a position to fill before he can ask the same offensive arrangement to produce a different result.

headline: The same form, filled out very differently
body:
Ordway and Son and Extremely Tight Ends have been given the same lineup form and arrived at substantially different conclusions. Jason currently has four running backs selected: Ashton Jeanty and Chuba Hubbard in the designated slots, D’Andre Swift and Aaron Jones at flex. Pete has four wide receivers: Chris Olave, Rashid Shaheed, Rome Odunze and DeMario Douglas. The flex designation has successfully avoided resolving the argument.

This is not quite last week’s leader coming back for an encore. Jason has Sam LaPorta selected instead of Mark Andrews, and Jones in the flex spot previously occupied by Cam Skattebo. Those two Week 6 slots combined for 0.9 in a win by 0.98. Pete’s running-back pair has changed too: Ollie Gordon and Zach Charbonnet are currently in, James Cook and Tyler Allgeier on the bench. Availability still needs checking before any of these arrangements can be treated as final.

Jason is 5–1. Pete is 4–2 and can put the two teams level on record by winning. There is no need to pretend that four backs or four receivers constitutes a universal theory of roster construction. It is enough that the league leader and one of his pursuers have used the two optional spaces so differently. We have asked them to select their best team. They would first like to disagree about its shape.

headline: You cannot buy back last Sunday
body:
Sherm has produced 18.79 more points than Roy this season and owns two fewer wins. Their meeting is therefore useful: Pollard Greens finally gets to compete against this particular five-and-one team instead of having its scoring total compared with it after everyone has gone home.

The available adjustment is also specific. Kyle Pitts is now in Sherm's tight-end slot, with Harold Fannin on the bench. Pitts's twenty-two last week would have reversed the loss to Norm; the new placement cannot retrieve that win. It purchases exposure to the next performance, which is not the same product. The current lineup also asks Roschon Johnson to share the running-back work with Quinshon Judkins.

Roy still lists C.J. Stroud and Chris Boswell, two additions that helped demolish Lloyd, and has Christian McCaffrey and Javonte Williams at running back. Sherm needs the best-scoring roster in LOOG to produce a winning allocation this week, not a more persuasive account of the previous six. A win narrows the gap between these teams to one game. That is a better use of the argument than continuing to accumulate evidence for it.

headline: Moving the label does not move the total
body:
Skatt has J.K. Dobbins at running back this week, where last week's score would have looked considerably more reassuring. There is one accounting problem: Dobbins was already in the lineup. Moving his 16.3 from flex to running back would not have added a point to the 108.34 that lost to Kush.

The meaningful change is the whole arrangement. The current sheet has Cam Skattebo on the bench, Dobbins alongside Kyren Williams, and Carnell Tate and Denzel Boston in the flex spots. The question is what this combination produces—not whether the running-back subtotal becomes more attractive. Last week's forty-seven-point deficit at two positions was real. It was not a separate match that Skatt could repair without affecting the other eight slots.

Danny supplies an unusually useful test. He currently has Breece Hall and Zach Charbonnet at running back, Jahmyr Gibbs in a flex, and last week's 24.9-point contributor Bhayshul Tuten unavailable during Jacksonville's bye. The lost contribution has to be replaced, not merely relocated. At two and four, Danny can join Skatt at three and four with a win. Skatt is rearranging the work; Danny must cover work the schedule has removed. The final ten-slot total will not care which problem was more irritating.

headline: He finally picked Daniels. Now Daniels is off.
body:
Norm finally started Jayden Daniels, got the points that helped him win, and now Washington has the week off. The quarterback argument had barely settled before the schedule removed its subject. Aaron Rodgers occupies Shake 'N Baker's Thursday quarterback slot. Whatever else Norm has learned, selecting last week's winning answer again is not among his options.

Across the matchup, All Ugly currently has Jared Goff at quarterback and Caleb Williams on the bench; I am not assigning a reason to that separate selection. Cody and Ferret's better discovery last week was distribution: eight starters reached double figures, nobody needed forty, and a 1.45-point win finally counted. The current arrangement has Woody Marks and Ollie Gordon at running back, with Dameon Pierce in a flex. Norm still has Chuba Hubbard and Tre Tucker selected, after those two supplied 54.6 in his last victory.

All Ugly can catch Shake 'N Baker at two and five. Norm can instead reach three and four and leave a two-win gap between them. I would like to see what survives from those victories when the exact lineups do not. In Norm's case, the little bye designation has settled one issue without argument. It has been rather less helpful about what to do next.

headline: The famous names are below the line
body:
Royrek's Thursday bench contains Justin Jefferson, Saquon Barkley and Lamar Jackson. Whatever ultimately determines their availability and placement, it makes the selected lineup an interesting place to look for the team. Kirk Cousins is at quarterback. Rhamondre Stevenson and Najee Harris occupy the running-back slots. The famous names cannot contribute from the lower half of the screen.

Route 22 is also carrying a recognizable bench, including James Cook during Buffalo’s bye and Rashee Rice. Its selected receivers are Tet McMillan and Xavier Worthy, the pair who supplied 30.9 in last week's win after the position produced five combined the week before. Brock Bowers is at tight end; Ryan Flournoy occupies a flex. The Clubhouse is three and three, with an opportunity to put another result behind that receiver improvement.

Royrek is two and four. Last week Matthew Golden and DK Metcalf supplied useful performances in a losing lineup; both are currently selected again. This is not an argument for any particular Thursday bench decision, whose remaining circumstances still need checking. It is an appointment between the people actually occupying the scoring slots. The reputations elsewhere on the roster may attend, but they will need to move before they can help.

headline: First place has a bench for this
body:
First place is not an exemption from the bye week. Kush has Ladd McConkey unavailable with the Chargers off, and Jaylin Noel is now among his selected receivers. Noel supplied 25.2 on the bench last Sunday. That does not promise a repeat. It does give the league leader something more useful than an explanation of why the usual man cannot play.

The current Hopkins sheet pairs Noel with George Pickens and has Sam LaPorta at tight end. Jonathan Taylor and Kenneth Walker remain the starting running backs, after their combined fifty-six covered a great deal of uneven work in the win over Skatt. I would not call Noel's selection a rebuke to a winning lineup. The schedule has made receiver depth an immediate assignment.

Matty has his own forced vacancy: Buffalo is off, so Josh Allen cannot help CeeDeep recover from its 1.45-point loss to All Ugly. Kyler Murray currently occupies the quarterback slot. Kush enters five and one; Matty is three and three. Both will have to defend their position with the people available, rather than the most impressive version of the roster. That is precisely what a bench is supposed to be for. It becomes much easier to assess when somebody has to leave it.

headline: The bench has received the minutes
body:
Emeka Egbuka is in Lloyd's flex this week. This is not enough to make last week's hundred-point defeat go away, but it does suggest the bench has received the minutes. The recap identified points sitting outside the lineup; at least one of those players is now being asked to make his case somewhere useful.

Dak Prescott remains the selected quarterback, while Trevor Lawrence is unavailable during Jacksonville's bye. Last week's alternative is not this week's solution. Lloyd is four and two, not obliged to replace every person associated with an ugly Sunday. Pat Freiermuth is selected at tight end, and Egbuka shares the flex work with Emanuel Wilson. The useful question is what those selections provide now, rather than how neatly they apologize for the previous score.

Kraft, at three and three, presents Puka Nacua and Nico Collins in the flex spots and Germie Bernard and Luther Burden at receiver. Bernard and Burden helped make last week's poor quarterback score survivable; Joe Burrow currently occupies that position. Final availability and selections still need checking. For Lloyd, this is a fairly specific examination: can the revised lineup keep up with several receivers at once? The apology does not have to be comprehensive. It does need to score.

headline: The distance to first
body:
Nipun has five wins to Sandy’s three. He has scored 22.30 more points across six weeks. The standings have made considerably more of the difference than the scoring column has. This week ZAYWATCH gets the leader directly, without having to persuade five other results to arrange themselves more helpfully.

Sandy’s Thursday selection puts Jared Goff at quarterback and Amon-Ra St. Brown in the flex, with Jordan Love on the bench. Nipun has C.J. Stroud selected and Aaron Jones in his flex. Those are the current arrangements, not the final guest list. Yahoo’s projections separate the teams by little more than a point; they are estimates, but they do not suggest an especially imposing border between first and seventh.

Last week Sandy lost by 3.38 and had no scoring reserve with which to construct an alternative victory. Nipun won without requiring another exceptional Christian Watson afternoon. One manager needs a different result; the other needs no grand demonstration. Five and one is a pleasantly economical way to enter a conversation.

headline: The part that worked
body:
Cody’s four receiving selections are still there: Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Luther Burden, Tet McMillan and Carnell Tate. Last week they supplied 62.5 between them, all four in double figures. Around that useful piece of construction, the Thursday lineup now pairs Ollie Gordon with Tyler Allgeier at running back. Dameon Pierce, who contributed thirteen to the win, is presently on the bench.

Andrew offers a different arrangement. Pat Freiermuth occupies tight end and Sam LaPorta the flex, with Kenneth Walker and David Montgomery at running back. The two-tight-end configuration is what Yahoo currently shows, not a claim that it will survive lock. Walker carried much of Andrew’s narrow Week 6 win. This time Cody needs the receiving group to keep doing useful work while the newly selected runners establish whether there is more to the afternoon.

Andrew is three and three; Cody is two and four. A Cody win brings them level on record. There is no need to rebuild the story around last week’s zero at tight end. Four players answered. The interesting question is who joins them.

headline: An asset moves upstairs
body:
Lamar Jackson has moved from Patrick’s Week 6 bench to the quarterback slot in the Thursday Week 7 capture. That is a lineup observation, not medical clearance or confirmation that he will play. Saquon Barkley remains on the bench. Our last column distinguished owning valuable names from being able to use them; the new lineup changes one side of that distinction, not both. There is also a definite repair: Jakobi Meyers remains selected at receiver during Jacksonville’s bye. Patrick needs a replacement there, independently of how the Lamar question resolves.

Rhamondre Stevenson and Kenny Gainwell remain selected at running back after combining for 6.5 last week. Across the matchup, Paul currently has D’Andre Swift and J.K. Dobbins selected. James Cook is on the bench during Buffalo’s verified bye: that is unavailable production, not evidence that Paul has lost confidence in him. Paul leads Sunday Crew in season scoring, so Patrick cannot plan around receiving the same modest target he missed last week.

At one and five, Patrick needs usable production rather than another impressive roster valuation. At four and two, Paul has more room, but last week’s win depended heavily on players outside his disappointing starting receiver trio. The practical question is narrow: which of the resources each manager owns can actually be put to work this Sunday?

headline: The other jobs
body:
Matt still has Patrick Mahomes selected and Tyler Shough on the bench. Last week Shough would have supplied another 15.48, and Matt would still have lost. This is an inconvenient result for anyone hoping to reduce the whole afternoon to a photograph of the wrong quarterback.

This week the more immediate problem is Omarion Hampton, still in Matt’s selected running-back pair while the Chargers are on bye. Blake Corum is on the bench. His availability and matchup need checking, but the vacancy in Hampton’s NFL schedule is settled. Matt’s two-tight-end arrangement—Isaiah Likely at tight end, Tucker Kraft in the flex—cannot make that running-back slot produce a game.

Runit’s Thursday lineup already has Aaron Rodgers selected with Josh Allen on the bench for Buffalo’s bye. He also has three running backs selected, which remains an agreeably complicated position for a team called RBs are Overrated. Runit is four and two, Matt two and four. Matt can reopen the Mahomes–Shough debate if useful. First, one of the other jobs needs somebody whose team is working.

headline: The quarterback has the week off
body:
I defended Drew’s record last week, and he immediately won with ninety points. I am prepared to retire the defense. Scrump has a more useful matter in front of it: Bijan Robinson and Jahmyr Gibbs are both selected at running back this Thursday, with Chris Godwin in the flex. Last week’s winning lineup did not need to be mistaken for the best version of this team.

Ravi has a less abstract problem than the schedule’s general injustice. Justin Herbert remains selected at quarterback, and the Chargers have a verified Week 7 bye. The retrieved roster contains no second quarterback. That is not evidence of negligence—this is a Thursday snapshot—but it makes the next move quite specific. Before evaluating whether the receivers can carry the team, Ravi needs a quarterback with a game.

His receiver configuration is already different: DeVonta Smith occupies one of the three receiver slots, Jameson Williams the flex. That department worked in last week’s loss; the rest did not. Ravi is three and three, Drew two and four, and a Scrump win puts them level. There will be time to argue about which record better describes its owner. First Ravi has a practical assignment and Drew has an opponent whose lineup is not finished.

headline: Tucker did not replace Boston
body:
Tre Tucker is selected for J Bird this Thursday. So is Denzel Boston. That matters because last week’s easy hindsight exercise put Tucker in Boston’s place and found another 24.2 points. Joe’s current lineup is not that substitution: Boston occupies a receiver slot, Tucker the flex. Chase Brown is now selected at running back, with Kendre Miller on the bench. The allocation has changed in more than one place.

Greg still shows Matthew Stafford at quarterback and Trevor Lawrence on the bench, but this is not a replay of last week’s decision. Jacksonville is on bye. Lawrence’s Week 6 advantage would have reversed Greg’s narrow loss; it supplies no Week 7 alternative. A correct review cannot simply sort the old points column and call it a forecast.

Joe has a separate, definite coverage issue: Tyler Bass is still selected at kicker during Buffalo’s bye. The seventeen Bass supplied last week cannot be carried forward. J Bird is three and three after three straight wins; Greg is four and two after consecutive losses. Joe’s revised receiving allocation is worth watching, but the next repeatable improvement is less glamorous: make sure every selected slot has a game to score in.
